timecoded_text_to_speech.text: There are a lot of disadvantages with using AI, but it's only if you let them be a disadvantage.
AI can get you 50% of the way there.
Sometimes even more, but the expectation that it can write an entire blog post,
or it can write social media posts and get you all the way there, is going to be a limiting factor.
If you can use AI as a creative tool and apply your unique vantage point to the problem you're solving,
it's going to be an amazing tool.
I think the biggest disadvantage to AI would be ignoring it or fearing it,
instead of figuring out how to use it.
Innovation has always happened throughout human history, and there's always two takes on it.
Full steam ahead, without any thought, to anything other than progress,
or on the flip side, just shrink back and ignore it and stick your head in the sand.
We don't even know all the ways that AI can be used, and we won't figure it out,
unless great people use it regularly and try to figure out how to use it in advance things that they're doing.
So I'd encourage you just be curious.
Figure out how you can use AI to do things that you do, and then ask yourself the question,
what can AI not do that I still need to do to make an awesome product for my client?
That type of curious questioning is going to help humanity chart a course into a new world,
where AI does a lot of stuff that we used to do, but we're still going to have a lot of stuff to do
to make the world a better place.
So let's figure it out.

youtube_description:
Ignoring AI is going to set you back more than if you just embrace it. 

We see two paths: full steam ahead, pushing boundaries. And retreating, hoping it'll fade away. 

AI's potential remains untapped; we won't discover until we dive in, experiment, and innovate. 

So...stay curious. See how AI can elevate your work, and ask yourself: What can't AI do that I offer to my clients? 🤔
